anchors.paper_title: Frontotemporal bursting supports human working memory
anchors.reason: The dataset README explicitly cites the candidate paper (DOI: 10.1016/j.neuroimage.2026.121718) as the associated publication, and the paper's title/abstract describe the specific data source (intracranial recordings) used.

metadata.methods_description: Intracranial EEG recordings were obtained from frontal (left and right middle frontal gyrus) and temporal (left and right middle temporal gyrus) regions during a load-3 object working memory task. Data underwent artifact rejection procedures at the single-trial level, with trial structure consisting of 1000 ms fixation, 1500 ms encoding, and 3998 ms delay periods. Trials were concatenated per channel and stored in EDF format with zero-padding for consistent array lengths across channels within subjects.

citation_details.title: Processing of different word list lengths during encoding and retrieval in Broca’s area
citation_details.author: Viktors Veliks, Aleksandrs Koļesovs, Juris Porozovs, Dmitrijs Igonins
citation_details.abstract: Broca's area is a region of the brain involved in the processing of verbal information, including memory encoding and retrieval. This study examined differences in the neural correlates of encoding and retrieval in Broca's area using word lists of varying lengths. Differences in the encoding and retrieval processes were assessed using word lists of different lengths: short (2-29), medium (30-59), and long (60-225) Latvian language nouns. In total, 23 participants completed the memory task. Each participant performed memory tasks with two short lists, two medium lists, and one long list, with varying list lengths within each diapason. We considered the activity of the F3 and F7 to represent our region of interest. We compared time-frequency (TF) data from encoding and retrieval across list lengths.
